Plai Laem is the north-east tip of Koh Samui, the headland between Big Buddha (Bang Rak) and Choeng Mon on the Route 4171 loop. It is home to Wat Plai Laem, with its 18-armed Guanyin on a lake, a string of resorts, villas and beach clubs, and it is about 5 minutes from the airport and minutes from the Big Buddha and Bang Rak piers for boats to Koh Phangan. The shore is mostly resort frontage facing Koh Phangan, and the water is shallow and variable, so for a proper swim most people drive 5 minutes to Choeng Mon.

Map

Plai Laem sits at the corner where the north coast turns south towards Choeng Mon. Big Buddha is on the Koh Fan islet causeway to the west, Wat Plai Laem about 1 km east of it, and Choeng Mon's bay just round the tip. Tongson Bay, a small sheltered cove, lies on the north side of the headland.

Wat Plai Laem and Big Buddha

The two most visited temples on Samui are 1 km apart, and together they take about 2 hours.

Wat Plai Laem

A bright Thai-Chinese temple complex built between 2004 and 2009 on a shallow lake. A white 18-armed Guanyin stands on a platform in the water, a large laughing Buddha (Phra Sangkachai) sits opposite, and an ordination hall decorated in ceramic tile appears to float between them. Catfish, carp and turtles crowd the edges when visitors feed them (fish food costs a few baht from machines). Entry is free and the grounds open about 06:00–18:00. Arrive around 08:00, before tour vans; cover shoulders and knees. Full guide: Wat Plai Laem.

Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai)

The golden seated Buddha on the Koh Fan islet, linked to the shore by a causeway, has been Samui's landmark for decades. Climb the dragon staircase for views over Bang Rak bay; shoes come off at the top. Free, about 07:00–18:30, with stalls and cafés at the base. See Big Buddha.

The beach: what it's really like

Plai Laem is not a classic swimming beach. The shore on the north side of the headland faces Koh Phangan across the bay and is mostly divided between resort frontages. The sand varies from narrow and coarse to rocky in places [check]. As at neighbouring Bang Rak, the water is shallow for a long way out and the seabed can be muddy or weedy at low tide [check]. Conditions differ from one resort to the next, so check the swimming at your hotel before you book if a sea swim matters. Many hotels here rely on their pools.

For a proper swim, the calmest bay on the island, Choeng Mon, is 5 minutes away by car, with soft sand and a sandbar to the islet of Koh Fan Noi at low tide. Tongson Bay, a small cove on the north side of the headland, is clear and shallow from December to April and rougher from May to October; the last stretch of road is sand.

The north-east tip catches the north-east monsoon from October to December, when the sea can be choppy and windy. Live sea and tide:

Beach clubs

The beach clubs along Bang Rak and Plai Laem face north across the bay, and they are built around the sunset: the sun drops behind the north coast while the sky glows over Koh Phangan. Clubs listed in the Bang Rak and Plai Laem area include:

  • Chi Samui: swim-up bar, sunset DJ sets and fire shows.
  • Tembo Beach Club: sunset DJ sets, tapas and happy-hour nights through the week.
  • Malika Beach Club and 79 Beach Club, the latter known for its New Year's Eve party.

Expect a minimum spend on day beds at weekends and in high season. Programmes change with the season, so check what's on before you go. For the island-wide scene, see Koh Samui beach clubs.

Staying in Plai Laem

Plai Laem mixes mid-range and upmarket resorts on the shore with private pool villas on the slopes. It suits:

  • Short stays and transit: the airport is about 5 minutes away, so it works for a first or last night.
  • Island-hoppers: the Big Buddha pier (Haad Rin Queen to Koh Phangan) and the Bang Rak piers for Lomprayah and Seatran boats are a few minutes' drive.
  • Full Moon Party nights: the shortest transfer on Samui to Haad Rin.
  • Villa groups: sea-view villas with pools, close to Choeng Mon's beach and Chaweng's restaurants (15 minutes).

The trade-offs: limited swimming at the shore, a quiet evening scene outside the beach clubs, and some aircraft noise, because planes approach and leave Samui Airport over the north-east. Ask your hotel if your room is under the flight path. Prices vary widely by resort; compare areas in where to stay on Koh Samui, or browse villas.

Food nearby

Resort restaurants and beach clubs cover the headland itself. For cheaper Thai food, Bang Rak has local restaurants along the bay and Plaza The Green Market near the Seatran pier, open daily from about 15:00 to 22:00. Choeng Mon's beach restaurants are 5 minutes away, and Fisherman's Village in Bophut, with the island's best dining street and its Friday walking street, is 10–15 minutes away.

How to get there

Plai Laem is on Route 4171, which leaves the ring road near the airport and loops around the north-east tip past Big Buddha, Plai Laem and Choeng Mon. Grab works well in this area. Taxis don't use meters, so agree the fare first.

Boats from the Big Buddha and Bang Rak piers

Several different piers along Bang Rak bay are all called "Bangrak pier", so always check the exact pier on your ticket. The Haad Rin Queen ferry leaves the Big Buddha pier for Haad Rin on Koh Phangan at 10:30 and 17:00 (about 50 minutes, 200 THB), and a Haad Rin Queen speedboat takes 25–30 minutes for 500 THB. Lomprayah runs about 10 sailings a day to Thong Sala from its own pier. Details in Big Buddha Beach and Koh Samui to Koh Phangan.

For the Full Moon Party, our shared Full Moon speedboat costs 1,400 THB return with hotel pickup from most areas, and a private Full Moon speedboat for up to 10 costs from 19,500 THB, on your own times. The next Full Moon Parties are on 24 November, 24 December and 31 December 2026. Entry at the party (about 200 THB) is paid on the beach; we sell the boats only.

Tours from Plai Laem

Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui, including Plai Laem. Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut (and other remote areas) add 400 THB per person, return.

  • Ang Thong speedboat tour: 1,800 THB (child 1,400 THB) plus the cash park fee; the park is closed 1 November–15 December 2026 and reopens on 16 December.
  • Pig Island speedboat: 1,450 THB (child 1,250 THB), every day of the year, including the Ang Thong closure.
  • Private speedboat charter: from 19,000 THB per boat for Koh Phangan's beaches, Pig Island or a sunset run.
